record.paper_title: Positive and free boundary solutions to singular nonlinear elliptic problems with absorption: an overview and open problems
record.original_question: For the singular nonlinear elliptic and free-boundary problems discussed in this survey, what multiplicity results remain valid when the diffusion term is replaced by other operators, including a general linear second-order elliptic operator, the p-Laplacian, Hamilton-Jacobi type operators, the Monge-Ampère operator, the bi-Laplacian, or operators arising in nonlinear systems or Schrödinger systems?

evidence.quote: Finally, in Section 5 we present a short list of some interesting open problems in the theory. Again, they concern principally the possible multiplicity of positive solutions and of free boundary solutions in general domains in R^N for N>1.

Multiplicity for different diffusion operators (not only a general linear second order operator or the p-Laplacian operator, but other nonlinear operators of Hamilton-Jacobi type, Monge-Ampère, bi-Laplacian, nonlinear systems, Schroedinger systems, etc.)

artifact.category_tag: singular semilinear elliptic equations with absorption
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as part of an explicit list of open problems in a survey on singular nonlinear elliptic problems with absorption. While partial results exist for the p-Laplacian and some linear second-order operators in special settings, a comprehensive multiplicity theory for free boundary / flat solutions covering Hamilton–Jacobi, Monge–Ampère, bi-Laplacian, and Schrödinger system diffusions remains open. No source was found establishing a complete resolution.

status_evidence.title: Positive and free boundary solutions to singular nonlinear elliptic problems with absorption (zbMATH)
status_evidence.snippet: Section 5 presents a short list of open problems concerning the possible multiplicity of positive solutions and of free boundary solutions, including multiplicity for different diffusion operators (general linear second order, p-Laplacian, Hamilton–Jacobi, Monge–Ampère, bi-Laplacian, nonlinear systems, Schrödinger systems).
status_evidence.claim: The multiplicity question across these alternative diffusion operators is explicitly listed as an open problem.
